values: most of the variance at document openings is token-specific and has no simple
concept behind it. Everywhere else the program predicts 0.
"""

READS = ()

TITLE_COLON = 3.27
CODE_OPENERS = set("/#%(*\\")


def opener_value(s):
    """Predicted activation for a document's first token, from its decoded text."""
    if s.startswith("<"):
        return 0.1
    if s.strip() == "":
        return -0.13
    c = s.lstrip(" ")
    if c[0] in CODE_OPENERS:
        return -0.07
    if c[0].isupper():
        return -0.18
    if c[0].isdigit():
        return 0.06
    if c[0].isalpha():
        return 0.04
    return 0.13


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    t = prefix.position
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    toks = prefix.token_strings
    if t == 0 or docs[t] != docs[t - 1]:
        return None, opener_value(toks[t])
    # the colon right after a document-opening "Title"
    opens_doc = t == 1 or docs[t - 1] != docs[t - 2]
    if opens_doc and toks[t - 1] == "Title" and toks[t] == ":":
        return None, TITLE_COLON
    return None, 0.0

mostly negative contribution from spelling format and broad word classes.
These class averages miss large differences between individual content words.

import regex
import wordnet
import wordfreq

    (-0.18, set('of in on at to by for from with into onto over under about '
                'after before between through during as'.split())),
    (-0.18, set('and or but if while when because although unless whether '
                'than so then'.split())),
    (-1.24, set('this that these those here there'.split())),
    (-0.11, set('am is are was were be been being have has had having '
                'do does did doing done'.split())),
    (0.94, set('can could may might must shall should will would cannot'.split())),
    (0.39, set('no not never neither nor'.split())),
    (-0.28, set('all any some every each both either many much more most few '
                'little other another such only'.split())),
)
PRONOUNS = set('i you he she it we they me him her us them my your his its '
               'our their'.split())
NOUN_CLASSES = (
    ('animal', -1.84),
    ('body', -2.03),
    ('artifact', -0.63),
    ('group', -1.11),
    ('phenomenon', -1.64),
)

        return -3.06 if s == '<|endoftext|>' else 0.91

        if '\t' in t:
            return 2.94
        if '\n' in t or '\r' in t:
            return 0.07
        return -0.93 if len(t) == 1 else 0.34
    if len(s) == 1 and s in '0123456789':
        return 1.41 - 0.687 * int(s) + 1.58 * (s == '0')
    if re.fullmatch(r'#+', s):
        return -5.30
    if re.match(r'^#\s*(include|define|ifdef|ifndef|endif|pragma)\b', s):
        return 3.32
    if s.startswith('//') and '\n' in t:
        return 5.19
    if s in (r'\n', r'\t', r'\r'):
        return 4.08
    if s == ',':
        return -0.19

        return -4.74 + 1.62 * space - 1.44 * title
    if word in ('a', 'an'):
        return -3.43 + 1.45 * space
    if word in PRONOUNS:
        return -3.62 + 1.98 * space - 0.55 * title
    for level, words in FUNCTION_WORDS:
        if word in words:

    value += 1.23 * ('\n' in t) + 1.48 * ('\t' in t)
    if re.fullmatch('[A-Za-z]+', s):

        value -= 0.84 * (not pos) + 1.18 * ('noun' in pos)
        value += 0.41 * ('verb' in pos) - 0.37 * ('adjective' in pos)
        value += 1.37 * ('adverb' in pos)
        categories = wordnet.categories(word)
        for category, offset in NOUN_CLASSES:
            value += offset * ('noun.' + category in categories)
        value += 0.62 * word.endswith('s') + 1.38 * word.endswith('ing')
    else:

    if (len(prefix.document_ids) > 1 and
            prefix.document_ids[-1] == prefix.document_ids[-2]):

during until since as than like about against toward towards beyond behind

less least much too so enough pretty really nearly almost fairly completely
totally absolutely entirely equally increasingly slightly significantly
substantially relatively exceptionally unusually moderately considerably
""".split())

""".split())

""".split())

CONJUNCTIONS = set('and or but nor yet'.split())

""".split())

"""Activation of layers.1.mlp.down_proj:5690, a document-start and whitespace-run feature.

Two things make this component move:

1. The first token of a document (the first token of a row, or the first token
   after an end-of-text marker) gets a large positive activation when it starts a
   word, about +15, and a small one when it is punctuation, a digit or a blank
   token, about +4. Later tokens of a document get nothing from this rule.

2. A blank token (spaces, tabs or no-break spaces only) that continues a run of the
   same blank character on the same line, as in indentation or column padding, gets
   a large negative activation: about -13 for a space after two or more spaces, -7
   for a space after one space, -5 for a tab after tabs, -10 for a no-break space
   after no-break spaces. A blank token after a newline gets nothing.

"""

NON_WORD_START = 4.0


def _is_blank(s):
    return len(s) > 0 and s.strip(" \t\r\n\xa0") == ""

    body = token.lstrip(" ")
    if not body:
        return NON_WORD_START
    first = body[0]
    if first.isalpha() or body.startswith("<|"):
        return WORD_START
    return NON_WORD_START


def _run_value(token, previous):
    # previous is a blank token on the same line; token continues its run
    if token == " " and previous.strip(" ") == "":
        return -13.0 if len(previous) >= 2 else -7.0
    if token == "\t" and previous.strip("\t") == "":
        return -5.0
    if token == "\xa0" and previous.strip("\xa0") == "":
        return -10.0
    return 0.0

    strings = prefix.token_strings
    token = strings[-1]
    if len(prefix) == 1 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        return carry, _doc_start_value(token)
    previous = strings[-2]
    if _is_blank(token) and _is_blank(previous):
        return carry, _run_value(token, previous)
    return carry, 0.0

roughly zero. Right after a document starts the response is stronger

interpunct pair "··" (a steady, moderate response of about 1.45), and on the colon of a
"Title:" header that opens a document (about 11, the largest responses in the data).

Compounds containing 头/頭 (一头, 回头, 点头 are high; 馒头, 额头, 摄像头 are near zero) are
left at 0: their responses are too mixed for one value, and predicting their average hurt
the model's next-token loss. Everything else is predicted as 0. Most of the remaining
variance is small, diffuse activity on ordinary tokens and on the first tokens of a
document, which this program does not describe.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS = ()

HEAD_CHARS = frozenset({"头", "頭"})   # the character for "head"
HEAD_WORDS = frozenset({"đầu"})        # Vietnamese "head"
DOTS = frozenset({"··"})               # interpunct pair

HEAD_VALUE = 5.6
WORD_VALUE = 3.5
DOT_VALUE = 1.45
TITLE_VALUE = 11.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if tok in HEAD_CHARS:
        return carry, HEAD_VALUE
    if tok in HEAD_WORDS:
        return carry, WORD_VALUE
    if tok in DOTS:
        return carry, DOT_VALUE
    # ":" right after a document's first token "Title", i.e. a "Title: ..." header at the top
    if tok == ":" and len(prefix) >= 2 and prefix.token_strings[-2] == "Title":
        docs = prefix.document_ids
        if len(docs) == 2 or docs[-3] != docs[-2]:
            return carry, TITLE_VALUE
    return carry, 0.0

"""Approximate a mixture of code, shell, and document-opening signals.

Identifier-like assignments have negative values. Shell switch names,
subcommands, and cd/grep have positive values; so does 'wx' following 'r'
(as in Unix permissions). The first token has separate rules for source
headers, selected personal pronouns, person-only WordNet nouns, By/by,
After/Before/When, and indentation. All other predictions are zero.

A 220-character tail recognizes local syntax, including escaped line breaks.
It resets with the document. Idiosyncratic word-dependent starts are omitted.
"""

import re
import wordnet

READS = ()

SHELL_TOOLS = frozenset('''git npm pnpm yarn cargo pip pip3 apt apt-get
python python3 node sed grep rg ls rm cp mv mkdir chmod chown wc curl
wget tar ffmpeg ssh make cmake gcc g++ rustc pytest tsc eslint docker kubectl
mvn gradle gem brew conda cat head tail sort uniq gunzip gzip perl bash sh
jest mocha pacman'''.split())
TOOL = re.compile(r'(?<![\w.])(?:' + '|'.join(map(re.escape, SHELL_TOOLS))
                  + r')(?![\w.])')
# These English words count as shell tools only in command-like phrases.
AMBIGUOUS_TOOL = re.compile(
    r'\bgo +(test|run|build|mod|fmt)\b|\bfind +[./~-]|\bset +-')
QUOTED_SWITCH = re.compile(
    r'''(?:^|[\s(\[{=,:])(?:\\*["'`])-{1,2}$|>-{1,2}$''')
SUBCOMMANDS = frozenset('''run test build install uninstall update upgrade
add remove delete get create apply status diff checkout restore reset clone
show log commit config stash fetch push pull init clean check lint fix'''.split())
DISPATCHERS = frozenset('''git npm pnpm yarn cargo go pip pip3 apt apt-get
kubectl docker gem brew conda'''.split())
COMMAND_END = re.compile(r'([A-Za-z0-9_+.-]+)$')
IDENTIFIER = re.compile(r'([A-Za-z_$][A-Za-z0-9_$]*)$')


def opening(token):
    if token == 'import':
        return 4.6
    if token == 'package':
        return 2.1
    if token == 'def':
        return -7.1
    if token in ('class', 'function'):
        return -2.5
    if token.startswith(('/*', '#!')):
        return 2.2
    if token == '##':
        return 2.0
    if token in ('He', 'She'):
        return -4.8
    if token in ('We', 'They'):
        return -2.7
    if token in ('By', 'by'):
        return -4.3
    if token in ('After', 'Before', 'When'):
        return -5.0
    person = token.isalpha() and token.istitle()
    if person and wordnet.categories(token) == {'noun.person'}:
        return -3.2
    indented = len(token) > 2 or '\t' in token
    if token.isspace() and '\n' not in token and indented:
        return -1.5
    return 0.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    new = carry is None or carry[0] != doc
    previous, recent = ('', '') if new else carry[1:]
    # Only subcommands need the complete preceding word, not a token fragment.
    subcommand = token.strip() in SUBCOMMANDS
    match = COMMAND_END.search(recent) if subcommand else None
    command = match[1] if match else ''
    value = 0.0
    if new:
        value = opening(token)
    elif token in (' =', ' :='):
        match = IDENTIFIER.search(recent)
        name = match[1] if match else ''
        if name:
            if name.isupper():
                value = -0.12
            elif token == ' :=':
                value = -0.60
            else:
                value = -0.43 if len(name) > 1 else -0.11
    elif token.startswith(' ') and command in DISPATCHERS and subcommand:
        if command == 'go':
            value = 0.0 if token.strip() == 'get' else 1.7
        else:
            packages = {'npm', 'pnpm', 'pip', 'pip3', 'apt-get', 'apt'}
            value = 2.5 if command in packages else 2.0
    elif token.strip() == 'cd':
        value = 0.8 if token == 'cd' else 0.34
    elif token.strip() == 'grep':
        value = 0.35 if token == 'grep' else 0.57
    elif token == 'wx' and recent.endswith('r'):
        value = 1.4
    elif previous.endswith('-') and token and token[0].isascii():
        # A spaced/quoted dash introduces a switch, not a hyphenated word.
        lead = previous.rstrip('-')
        spaced = lead.isspace()
        quoted = bool(QUOTED_SWITCH.search(recent))
        # Quoted switch names can also appear in argument lists or HTML.
        if token[0].isalpha() and (spaced or quoted):
            line = recent.rsplit('\n', 1)[-1]
            shell = bool(TOOL.search(line) or AMBIGUOUS_TOOL.search(line))
            if shell:
                value = 1.35 if recent.endswith('--') else 1.95
            elif quoted:
                value = 0.8 if recent.endswith('--') else 1.6
            elif previous == ' --':
                value = 1.2
    # Shell snippets are often embedded in strings with escaped line breaks.
    recent = (recent + token).replace('\\n', '\n').replace('\\t', '\t')
    return (doc, token, recent[-220:]), value

"""Activation of layers.1.mlp.down_proj:5693 (a down-projection feature).

It is mostly silent, but it has two strong, readable regimes:

1. First token of a document (the first token after <|endoftext|>, or the first token of a row).
   Here the activation depends only on the token itself. Person names and subject pronouns
   (He, She, Thomas, Brian...) push it strongly negative. Imperative UI/instruction verbs
   (Show, Select, Click, Welcome...) and code/markup starters (import, package, FROM, ##)
   push it positive. Other capitalised words are mildly negative.
2. Inside a line of shell command, the letter right after a command-line flag dash
   (python -m, sed -i, wc -l, ssh-keygen -R) is positive. Assignment operators are mildly
   negative (" =" and Go's " :=").
Everything else predicts 0.
"""

READS = ()

NAMES = set(
    """John Mary James Robert Michael William David Richard Joseph Thomas Charles Daniel Matthew
    Anthony Mark Paul Steven Andrew Kevin Brian Gary Jose Maria Jennifer Linda Elizabeth Susan
    Jessica Sarah Karen Nancy Lisa Michelle Emily Anna Laura Peter Adam Edward Ron Louis Jack Tom
    Bob Tim Dave Jim Ben Chris Mike Steve Sam Alex Nick""".split()
)
PRONOUNS = set("He She They We I You It There Their His Her By After Before When While".split())
INSTRUCTIONS = set(
    """Show Select Click Generate Set Give See Welcome More Next First New Get Make Use Read Learn
    Find Try Check Add Create Install Run Enter Choose Save Open""".split()
)
CODE_START = set("import export package FROM JOIN from include # ## ### ** /* #!/".split())
SHELL_WORDS = set(
    """cd npm pip pip3 git cargo python python3 sed grep curl apt apt-get docker ssh ssh-keygen
    ssh-keyscan ffmpeg wc chown ls make tar rm cp mkdir yarn sudo export bash node chmod pytest wget
    kubectl go gem brew find cat xargs""".split()
)
DASHES = {"-", "--", " -", " --"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = tok.strip()
    if prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        if word in NAMES or word in PRONOUNS:
            value = -2.5
        elif word in INSTRUCTIONS or word in CODE_START:
            value = 1.5
        elif word[:1].isupper():
            value = -0.4
        else:
            value = -0.15
        return {"shell": False}, value
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2]
    shell = carry["shell"] if carry else False
    if "\n" in tok:
        shell = False
    if word in SHELL_WORDS:
        shell = True
    if prev in DASHES and word.isalpha() and word.isascii() and shell:
        value = 1.0
    elif tok == " :=":
        value = -0.63
    elif tok == " =":
        value = -0.24
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return {"shell": shell}, value

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:5695 -- a "k inside a word" detector.

The component reads the letter k (or Cyrillic к) when it is inside a word, not at its start,
and reacts to the letters just before it:

- A "k" that is a word piece of its own (ST|K|33, longputtCh|k|Total, Mos|k|va):
  positive after a consonant (about +1); negative after a vowel (about -0.8);
  strongly negative (about -4) after "e" ("-ek" in Turkish, Polish, Hungarian, Swedish names
  and words such as bö|cek|leri, order|bek|räft).
- A word piece ending in "k": "-ek" after a consonant (-2.5) is the big negative case, "-ak", "-ok",
  "-ik" after a consonant are mildly negative (-0.5), and "ee"+k (English "leek", "seek") is zero.
- Everything else, which is almost every token, predicts 0.

Only the text so far is read, so the program is causal.
"""

READS = ()

VOWELS = set("aeiouyäöüáéíóúőűàèìòùâêîôûəăışěůý" "аеёиоуыэюя")
E_LETTERS = set("eе")  # Latin and Cyrillic e


def is_letter(c):
    return c is not None and c.isalpha()


def is_consonant(c):
    return is_letter(c) and c not in VOWELS


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    piece = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    text = prefix.text_prefixes[prefix.position].lower()
    if not text.endswith(("k", "к")):
        return carry, 0.0
    before = text[-2] if len(text) > 1 else None  # letter before the k
    before2 = text[-3] if len(text) > 2 else None  # letter before that one
    if not is_letter(before):  # a k that starts a word
        return carry, 0.0
    if piece in ("k", "к"):  # the k is a piece of its own
        if before in E_LETTERS:
            value = -4.0
        elif before in VOWELS:
            value = -0.8
        else:
            value = 1.0
    elif before in E_LETTERS:  # "...ek" or "...eek"
        value = -2.5 if is_consonant(before2) else 0.0
    elif before in VOWELS and is_consonant(before2):  # "...ak", "...ok", "...ik"
        value = -0.5
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return carry, value
